headline: context identity resolved on discriminative genes: A is clearly Jurkat-like (r=0.65 vs next best 0.40), B weakly RPE1-leaning (0.37), C unresolved/hESC-leaning — global Pearson is inflated by housekeeping+assay similarity and misleads

audit_flags.message: Global Pearson (all genes) ranks hESC first for every context, but hESC shares the Perturb-seq assay with the 2026 controls — housekeeping+protocol similarity inflates it; the discriminative-gene metric is the decision signal

interpretation: Context A: Jurkat/T-cell confirmed on top-2000 context-discriminative genes (0.649), consistent with the marker analysis (CD3D/CD8A/TRAC rank ~0.84). The Nadig 2024 Jurkat screen (2,393 essential targets) is the right prior source for A
Context B: weak RPE1 lean (0.369 vs hESC 0.357) — consistent with fibro/epi markers but not decisive; the RPE1 essential arm may still help its covered targets
Context C: unresolved; hESC-leaning on discriminative genes (0.379)
The Nadig dataset covers Jurkat AND HepG2 over the same 2,393-target essential design — a per-context prior-source dispatch is now the concrete next experiment
next_steps: k013: per-context prior dispatch — Jurkat-arm deltas for context A, RPE1-arm for B, existing K562/Atlas for C (needs build_context_predictions to accept per-context delta dicts)
Check 2026 panel coverage of the Nadig/RPE1 essential-scale target sets before building (essential-scale ~2,393 targets; panel overlap unknown)
